Empirical

/em-PEER-ih-kul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Empirical means based on observation, experience, or experiment rather than on theory alone — capable of being tested

Empirical means based on observation, experience, or experiment rather than on theory alone — capable of being tested

Worked Example

The marine ecologist's claim that the kelp forest was recovering rested on <strong style="color:var(--accent);">empirical</strong> measurements she had logged every week for two years.

Her claim is grounded in direct, repeated observation — two years of weekly measurements — rather than a guess or a theory, which is what makes the support empirical.

How Empirical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

observed

observed: noted directly through watching or measuring

evidence-based

evidence-based: grounded in collected facts

experimental

experimental: derived from controlled tests

Antonyms

conjectural

conjectural: based on guesswork

untested

untested: not yet checked against reality

How Strong Is It? — anecdotal → empirical → ironclad

anecdotal vs. empirical

anecdotal vs. empirical: Anecdotal is weaker than empirical — a few customers' scattered stories can't match systematically collected data.

ironclad vs. empirical

ironclad vs. empirical: Ironclad goes beyond empirical — empirical findings rest on evidence, but ironclad proof has already survived every challenge thrown at it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — em-

Prefix — em-: in, within (Greek en-)

Root — pir-

Root — pir-: trial, test, attempt (from Greek peira, 'trial' — respelled -pir- in English)

Suffix — -ical

Suffix — -ical: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: Em- ('in,' from Greek en-) + pir- (trial, test — Greek peira, respelled -pir- in English) + -ical (relating to) builds the literal sense 'found in trial' — empirical knowledge is what you learn by testing and experiencing, not by reasoning alone.

Use the root in a new word: expertise

Use the root in a new word: expertise: Years of fieldwork gave the mountain guide an expertise that no textbook could supply — knowledge earned through trial after trial.

Root Check

Word Choice

Academic / scientific

Empirical describes evidence, data, studies, and methods — anything grounded in observation or experiment ('empirical evidence,' 'an empirical study'). Don't confuse it with imperial ('relating to an empire'), a sound-alike built on a completely unrelated root. And note that its unit-mate hypothetical is its opposite in spirit: empirical means tested against reality; hypothetical means assumed without testing.
